audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer twice tells the player to use "Abyssal Voyage" — once as a level-6 tool ("Your Abyssal Voyage at 6 is not a duel tool here; use it to threaten teleport plays") and once as the late-game win condition ("Abyssal Voyage becomes your most valuable ability").
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's PRE-REWORK ultimate (the long-range two-man taxi). It does not exist on the live champion. The live W is Abyssal Dive — a 1000-1200 range dive that knocks up on arrival, 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown — and it is available from level 2, not 6. Level 6 is Devour (R). A player told to 'threaten teleport plays' with an ability that no longer exists is being handed a plan they physically cannot execute.
audit.corrected: At 6 the new ability is Devour, usable on an enemy champion only at three An Acquired Taste stacks; on an ally it shields instead. Abyssal Dive is the engage/entry tool, and its knockup damage itself applies a stack of An Acquired Taste.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (DDragon 16.15.1) — W: Abyssal Dive, R: Devour; passive: 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] claims "at 5 stacks of Hallowed Mist she threatens a full Snip Snip! burst".
audit.why: Hallowed Mist has no stack mechanic of any kind — it is a single zone cast that makes Gwen untargetable to enemies outside it. Neither A Thousand Cuts nor Snip Snip! stacks to 5 either (Snip Snip! is up to 6 snips in one cast). The threat is invented. The real reason short trades stop paying at 4-5 is that Snip Snip! deals TRUE damage down its centre line, which Thick Skin's grey health and any amount of armour/MR do nothing about.
audit.corrected: Snip Snip!'s centre-line true damage is the mechanism, not a stack count.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gwen.json — W Hallowed Mist: 'summons mist that protects her... can only be targeted by enemies who enter the mist' (no stacks); Q Snip Snip!: 'deals true damage to units in the center'

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeats "trade around Hallowed Mist's cooldown" in five separate places but never once states what that cooldown is, so the advice is unactionable.
audit.why: Hallowed Mist is 22/21/20/19/18s — by a wide margin the longest cooldown in Gwen's laning kit (Q is 6.5 down to 3.5, E is 13 down to 11). At the levels where this matters (4-5) it is normally still rank 1 at 22s. That number is the entire matchup: a baited W is a 22-second window in which Tahm Kench's whole pattern works.
audit.corrected: State the 22s rank-1 figure at the points where the text tells the player to wait for the mist.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] says Gwen will "step back out of your Q range" after her E dash.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is 900 range; Skip 'n Slash is a 400-range dash. She cannot dash out of a 900-range Q — that is not the threat. The actual threat in Skip 'n Slash is that it grants bonus ATTACK RANGE along with the attack speed and on-hit magic damage, so during the buff she out-ranges Tahm Kench's autos and can keep hitting him while he cannot hit back to build stacks.
audit.corrected: Name the bonus attack range, and frame the disengage against the third An Acquired Taste stack rather than against Q range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gwen.json — E Skip 'n Slash: 'gains Attack Speed, attack range, and magic damage On-Hit'; range 400. champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Q range 900

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] justifies the level-2 window with "Hallowed Mist is not yet leveled enough to blank your Q".
audit.why: There is no partial-leveling effect on Hallowed Mist's untargetability — rank only changes cooldown and duration, not whether it works. Either she has the point in W or she does not. The honest reason the level-2 window exists is the raw cooldown length if she has already spent it.
audit.corrected: Replace the fake scaling reason with the 22s rank-1 cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gwen.json — W description contains no rank-gated targeting clause

audit.why: MR-first plus anti-heal is right here and is already stated. Gwen's damage that matters is magic (A Thousand Cuts on-hit, Skip 'n Slash on-hit, Needlework) and her passive heals her off champion damage, so Grievous Wounds is genuinely core rather than boilerplate. Left alone.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gwen.json — P A Thousand Cuts flags: heal; _missing-interactions.json rules needs-antiheal + onhit-itemization for tahmkench vs gwen

audit.why: 48.97% over 727 games. I checked whether diff/diffRating should move and deliberately left them: across all 71 Tahm Kench entries the diff scale is not win-rate-mapped (HARD 8.5 is also given to Teemo at 54.57% and Cassiopeia at 54.75%, both lanes Tahm Kench wins), so it reads as a difficulty-to-pilot scale. Gwen genuinely is hard to pilot against. No principled basis to change it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are her runway: Gwen's E gives her the repositioning to dodge your stacking pattern and her Snip Snip! scissors snips shred through Thick Skin grey health before you can heal it back in combat. Respect the mist — do not throw Q into Hallowed Mist, because abilities that originate outside the mist simply do not hit her. Play for CS and watch for the Hallowed Mist cooldown. At 6 her R (Needlework) pokes you down at range and chips your grey-health reserve, which means activating E for the shield becomes harder. Your Abyssal Voyage at 6 is not a duel tool here; use it to threaten teleport plays and keep yourself relevant globally rather than fighting a losing 1v1.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are her runway: Gwen's E gives her the repositioning to dodge your stacking pattern and her Snip Snip! scissors snips shred through Thick Skin grey health before you can heal it back in combat. Respect the mist — do not throw Q into Hallowed Mist, because abilities that originate outside the mist simply do not hit her. It is 22s at rank 1, so a mist she wastes is a real window. At 6 her R (Needlework) pokes you down at range and chips your grey-health reserve, which means activating E for the shield becomes harder. Your 6 is Devour, not a duel tool: at three An Acquired Taste stacks it removes Gwen from a fight, and on an ally it shields them out of Needlework.

edits.before: At first item Gwen's Riftmaker true damage eats through your tankiness in a way poke damage never does — the grey-health buffer Thick Skin builds up gets burned off by sustained Snip Snip! combos, and you cannot out-heal percent-max-health damage. Your job shifts to being an immovable frontline: Q-stun and Devour whoever walks at your carries, not Gwen herself. If you are forced to deal with her, wait for a window where Hallowed Mist is down and your whole team can collapse — her W makes her a nightmare to solo-kill at two items. Abyssal Voyage becomes your most valuable ability: use it to arrive in teamfights with stacks already building on the nearest target, and let your team clean up while Gwen scales in the sidelane.
edits.after: At first item Gwen's Riftmaker true damage eats through your tankiness in a way poke damage never does — the grey-health buffer Thick Skin builds up gets burned off by sustained Snip Snip! combos, and you cannot out-heal percent-max-health damage. Your job shifts to being an immovable frontline: Q-stun and Devour whoever walks at your carries, not Gwen herself. If you are forced to deal with her, wait for a window where Hallowed Mist is down and your whole team can collapse — her W makes her a nightmare to solo-kill at two items. Abyssal Dive is your entry: the knockup lands a stack on her carry, and Devour spent shielding a caught ally usually beats eating Gwen while she scales in the sidelane.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks unlock the Q stun — bait Gwen into a short trade, stack up, then Q-stun into Devour before she can pop Hallowed Mist.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks unlock the Q stun — bait Gwen into a short trade, stack up, then stun her out of the mist. Devour is your 6, not yet.

edits.before: Gwen's E dash lets her reposition out of your stacking range freely; at 5 stacks of Hallowed Mist she threatens a full Snip Snip! burst you cannot prevent with Thick Skin alone.
edits.after: Gwen's E dash lets her reposition out of your stacking range freely; Snip Snip!'s centre-line true damage cuts Thick Skin grey health that no armour or MR stops, so short trades stop paying.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online and Hallowed Mist is not yet leveled enough to blank your Q — land the stun and punish her commitment.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online and Hallowed Mist costs her a 22s cooldown at rank 1 — if she burns it early, stun her and punish.

edits.before: Dash in with E for attack-speed burst, then step back out of your Q range before you reach three stacks
edits.after: Dash in with E for attack speed and bonus range, then step out before your third An Acquired Taste stack lands

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Hallowed Mist's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane-control window: Hallowed Mist is 22s at rank 1, so bait it, then stack and stun. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.

notes: SITE-WIDE BUG, NOT LIMITED TO THIS MATCHUP: the string "Abyssal Voyage" appears in champ-data/content/tahmkench.js in matchups I do not own (I saw it in the aatrox entry too, and it is the level-6 / late-game advice in gwen). Abyssal Voyage was removed from Tahm Kench in the 2021 rework — the live W is Abyssal Dive and the live R is Devour. Recommend a grep for "Abyssal Voyage" across all tahmkench files and a sweep by whoever owns those slices; the packet's suspectNames checker did NOT flag it, because it only compares against near-miss spellings of names that DO exist.
